primary_claim: OthelloGPT's attention heads implement a 'Previous Color Circuit' that copies each tile's color forward from the most recent move at which it was flipped, reconstructing the probed board state with 0.818 accuracy, while a competing hypothesis that monosemantic MLP neurons implement discrete flipping rules failed an ablation test.

effect.metric: reconstruction accuracy of previous-color-circuit probe vs real attention output
effect.value: 0.818 overall (up to 0.97 for specific layer/position/tile combinations)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Provides mild evidence against the theory in 'OthelloGPT learned a bag of heuristics' that individual neurons perform interpretable discrete rules, though the author notes only a specific set of rules was tested
stated_future_work: Reproduce the flipping-circuit ablation experiment on a smaller scale (focusing on just one tile/rule) and investigate cases where the ablation setup fails to predict tile flips
limitations_stated: Only tested a very specific set of rules for the flipping circuit hypothesis
There's a chance of a bug in the code, since only one example was tested thoroughly
Should have gathered stronger evidence before running the large ablation experiment
quote: I think the results show that the previous color circuit is meaningful. But the model actually does something more complicated, so it's better thought of as a rough approximation of what the attention layers are doing.
